subject: POC readiness & model plan — Orion Retail (next steps & owners)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@orionretail.com>, Miguel Alvarez <miguel.alvarez@orionretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC readiness & model plan — Orion Retail (next steps & owners)

Hi Lina / Miguel,

Thanks again for the call today — great context on the conversational search pilot and the Spanish/Portuguese customer channel volumes. Below is a compact POC readiness checklist and the proposed model paths so we can lock timelines and owners. Please flag anything missing.

High-level goal:
- 6-week trial to validate retrieval-augmented conversation (FAQ + product catalog) with Spanish and Portuguese fallback into English when needed. Success metric = end-to-end F1 and a subjective NPS-style quality score from pilot users (see matrix attached).

Proposed model roster for trial (primary -> fallback):
- Primary: Mistral-Instruct-7B (quantized) — low-latency, good L2 performance for instruction tuning.
- Secondary (higher-accuracy): Llama-2-13B Q4 (8-bit quant) — for escalations and higher-complexity responses.
- Fallback: OpenAssistant/oasst-sft-6-llama2 (safety-tuned) — conservative responses for sensitive queries.

Multilingual approach:
- Default routing: Spanish/Portuguese -> Mistral-Instruct-7B tuned on 2k localized examples.
- If hallucination risk > threshold or privacy-sensitive data detected -> promote request to Llama-2-13B.
- If model confidence low -> return a safe fallback prompt and surface to human review.

Success criteria (acceptance):
- Quantitative: 0.65+ retrieval-response F1 on curated test set (Spanish + Portuguese) and <6% harmful/incorrect factuals measured on 200 sampled interactions.
- Qualitative: Pilot team average quality rating >=4/5 on 50 annotated cases.
- Latency: p50 < 350ms, p95 < 900ms for Spanish baseline queries.

Timeline (target):
- Week 0 (this week): kick-off, data deliverables, access & security checklist.
- Week 1: ingest sample prompts and product catalog; baseline eval on our infra.
- Week 2–3: model tuning, quantization profile testing, prefix caching config.
- Week 4: internal QA + pilot deployment to 10 agents.
- Week 5–6: iterate on failures, run acceptance evaluation, decision point.

Ownership (initial):
- PM / Account lead: Tessa Morgan — overall coordination and acceptance decision.
- Solutions / Eval lead: Marissa Cole — model shortlist tuning, eval rubric, test harness.
- Commercial / SLOs: Ben Carter — SLA/cost tradeoffs and billing guardrails.

Open asks for Orion:
1) Shared sample of 300 Spanish + 150 Portuguese queries (anonymized) — filename pattern recommended: sample_prompts_multilang.csv.
2) Confirmation on data retention constraints and whether we can cache prefix KV between agent sessions.
3) Who will be the pilot decision reviewer on your side for acceptance?

Attachments: POC-success-matrix.xlsx (contains evaluation rubrics + suggested guardrails), sample_prompts_multilang.csv (example prompts).

If this looks good, we’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff tomorrow at 10am PT with Marissa to walk through the matrix and confirm the security checklist.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0179
https://redwood.com
From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@orionretail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Alvarez <miguel.alvarez@orionretail.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: POC readiness & model plan — Orion Retail (next steps & owners)

Hi Tessa — thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers:
- We can provide the anonymized prompt set by EOD Wednesday (will include intent labels).
- Data retention: we need logs retained for 90 days and a paper trail that model outputs are not stored beyond session unless explicitly flagged. KV caching between agent sessions is allowed if encrypted; we use Vault for keys.
- Acceptance reviewer: I’ll act as primary reviewer; Miguel will be backup and our CS lead Laura will join the demo acceptance.

Spanish/Portuguese coverage is essential — roughly 60% Spanish, 30% Portuguese, 10% other. The fallback-to-English behavior should preserve SKU references and not translate product IDs.

Kickoff tomorrow 10am PT works for us. Looking forward to the matrix.

—Lina
Head of Conversational Experience | Orion Retail
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@orionretail.com>, Miguel Alvarez <miguel.alvarez@orionretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC readiness & model plan — Orion Retail (next steps & owners)

Thanks all — I’ll own the evaluation harness and the acceptance rubric (see attachment: POC-success-matrix.xlsx). A few notes and tweaks from the engineering perspective:

1) Test harness & datasets:
- Please include examples where customer provides partial IDs or emojis — these are high-failure modes.
- We’ll create a 200-case labeled holdout with a 60/30/10 language split to mirror production.

2) Model configurations to validate (we’ll run A/B):
- Config A: Mistral-Instruct-7B (int8) + retrieval top-5, answer synthesis.
- Config B: Llama-2-13B (8-bit) with same retrieval but stricter hallucination detection.
- Safety Mode: OpenAssistant-oasst-sft-6-llama2 as conservative response path.

3) Quantization and perf notes:
- We’ll benchmark 4-bit vs 8-bit quant on the key intents; if 4-bit drops accuracy >3 points we keep 8-bit.

4) Ownership checklist (action items):
- Marissa: build harness & baseline eval — deliver by Fri (2027-06-25).
- Ben: prepare a cost estimate for both configurations and p95 latency SLOs by Thu (2027-06-24).
- Tessa: gather signed NDA + confirm pilot decision reviewers on your side — Lina confirmed.

5) Security note:
- Please share your SOC2 or security questionnaire; we will provide redacted network diagram (attached: network-arch-diag.png) and the minimal required access scope.

I’ll host the kickoff demo tomorrow 10am PT and run through the matrix; I’ll also walk through how we tag low-confidence answers for human review.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Lina: we’ll expect sample_prompts_multilang.csv by EOD Wed and your SOC2 questionnaire via the secure upload link in my calendar invite.

Tessa
